note: Robot-made burgers (San Francisco), founded as Momentum Machines (2009, incorporated 2012) and renamed Creator in 2017; the base row already absorbed momentum-machines. Backed by GV, Khosla Ventures and Root Ventures, and it 'raised at least $18.3 million in 2017' per its filing (TechCrunch, 2018-06-21); its Form Ds ($345K from 2013-03-28, $18.4M from 2017-05-26 with Khosla's Sven Strohband a director, $13.0M from 2021-06-29 as Creator, Inc.) name no GV director, and no source read names the round GV entered, so the stage is undetermined. Status follows the Khosla row (closed permanently in 2023); the restaurant reopened in Daly City in August 2021 (San Francisco Chronicle) and no later operating trace was found.

Mobile app performance monitoring (San Francisco), renamed Apteligent; VMware announced its acquisition on 2017-05-15 (Wikipedia, Apteligent). Google Ventures was in the seed announced 2011-07-13 with Kleiner Perkins, Opus, Shasta and AOL Ventures ($1.2M; TechCrunch), re-upped in the $5.5M Series A of June 2012 with Opus and Shasta (TechCrunch, 2012-06-01), and led the $12M Series B of March 2013 (TechCrunch). The named Series A graduates the seed.

funding_rounds.lead: Opus Capital; Shasta Ventures; Google Ventures

note: DJZ, Seth Goldstein's electronic dance music media company (launched October 2012), and its mobile DJ app Crossfader are one company: 'Crossfader was created by Seth Goldstein's DJZ team' (TechCrunch, 2014-06-27); the base carries both rows (djz, crossfader). GV's round: DJZ launched 'with $1 million in funding' from Kleiner Perkins, Google Ventures, Index, True, Troy Carter and Shari Redstone (TechCrunch, 2012-10-31), its first round and seed-sized for 2012 (model: Seed, medium); Crossfader later took $2M from Shawn Gruver and Telegraph Hill Capital. No source read gives the company's fate (crossfader.fm no longer answers), so status is unknown, and none places its office. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

DJZ, Seth Goldstein's electronic dance music media company (launched October 2012), and its mobile DJ app Crossfader are one company: 'Crossfader was created by Seth Goldstein's DJZ team' (TechCrunch, 2014-06-27); the base carries both rows (djz, crossfader). GV's round: DJZ launched 'with $1 million in funding' from Kleiner Perkins, Google Ventures, Index, True, Troy Carter and Shari Redstone (TechCrunch, 2012-10-31), its first round and seed-sized for 2012 (model: Seed, medium); Crossfader later took $2M from Shawn Gruver and Telegraph Hill Capital. No source read gives the company's fate (crossfader.fm no longer answers), so status is unknown, and none places its office. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Marketplace for custom-made goods (Lechmere Square, Cambridge MA). 'In November 2011, CustomMade raised $2.1 million in Series A funding from First Round Capital, Google Ventures, and others', and Google Ventures co-led the $4M round of April 2012 (Wikipedia; Boston Business Journal headline, 2012-04-30). Status: Wikipedia says Wayfair acquired the business on 2015-05-21 (Woodworking Network's headline frames it as Wayfair hiring its staff while CustomMade retrenched), and in May 2017 the founder re-purchased the business out of foreclosure with WTI; custommade.com still trades as a custom jeweler (read 2026-09-28). A sale with a successor entity reads acquired with this note. The First Round row reads defunct ('wound down after 2018', uncited); this row holds the cited sale.

Authentication as a service, 'born as Shopobot' (an AngelPad price-tracking startup). Shopobot 'raised an undisclosed amount of seed funding from Google Ventures, AOL Ventures' and others (TechCrunch, 2011-06-16); the company's own farewell calls Google Ventures 'our first major investor' and says 'DailyCred ended all public APIs and services December 31st, 2020' (dailycred.com, read 2026-09-28). No source read places its office. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Collaborative data analysis (San Francisco), founded 2013 by Wes McKinney (pandas) and Chang She. It raised '$1.7 million in very early stage funding' from Accel, Google Ventures, a16z's seed fund, SV Angel and Ludlow (TechCrunch, 2014-05-20): its only round, unnamed, seed-sized (model: Seed). Cloudera acquired its technology assets and team on 2014-09-30 and shut the service (VentureBeat), an announced acquisition, so acquired; the a16z row reads defunct, and this row holds the cited acquisition. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Tech-talent marketplace. DeveloperAuction rebranded as Hired.com in September 2013 (TechCrunch, 2013-09-17), so developer-auction and hired are one company. GV's round: DeveloperAuction 'raised $2.7 million from NEA, Sierra Ventures, Crosslink Capital, Google Ventures' and others in March 2013 (TechCrunch, 2013-03-14); the round is unnamed and sits above the era's seed ceiling, and the next filing ($14.98M sold from 2014-11-25, Hired, Inc., San Francisco) names no round either, so the stage is undetermined. Vettery, part of the Adecco Group, acquired Hired in November 2020 (TechCrunch, 2020-11-23; Wikipedia). City: San Francisco, its Form D address.

Tech-talent marketplace. DeveloperAuction rebranded as Hired.com in September 2013 (TechCrunch, 2013-09-17), so developer-auction and hired are one company. GV's round: DeveloperAuction 'raised $2.7 million from NEA, Sierra Ventures, Crosslink Capital, Google Ventures' and others in March 2013 (TechCrunch, 2013-03-14); the round is unnamed and sits above the era's seed ceiling, and the next filing ($14.98M sold from 2014-11-25, Hired, Inc., San Francisco) names no round either, so the stage is undetermined. Vettery, part of the Adecco Group, acquired Hired in November 2020 (TechCrunch, 2020-11-23; Wikipedia). City: San Francisco, its Form D address.

Licensed social and mobile games (Game of Thrones Ascent, Star Trek Timelines), Framingham MA (Worcester Business Journal, 2016). It sold its games, reorganized and relaunched as Beamable, a live-game services platform (GamesIndustry.biz, 2020-04-22). 'Skillz acquired Beamable in January 2026' (Wikipedia, Jon Radoff); Skillz's own release of 2026-02-04 says it acquired Beamable's technology (Business Wire: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260204161246/en/Skillz-Acquires-Beamables-Technology-to-Accelerate-Platform-Innovation-Expand-Developer-Capabilities), a purchase of the product, which reads acquired. City: Boston, Beamable's address on its 2022 Form D (the last before the sale; Framingham through 2021). Rounds: a $3.2M Series A, which its Form D tranches of 2013-14 ($771K, $820K, $1.62M) add up to, and an $8.5M Series B led by GrandBanks and Romulus (TechCrunch, 2017-02-02; Form D from 2017-01-26); no filing names a GV director and no source read names the round GV entered, so the stage is undetermined.

Friend-finding and meet-up app (CEO Nick Bicanic), a Vancouver BC company ('EchoEcho: Vancouver company personalizes location-based service', Vancouver Sun, 2011-03-10). 'Last September, EchoEcho raised $750,000 from Google Ventures, UK-based venture firm PROfounders and Don Dodge', then another $750K led by Bullpen Capital (TechCrunch, 2012-05-07; Reuters headline, 2011-09-09): GV's round is the company's first, unnamed and seed-sized (model: Seed). No source read gives its fate; Bicanic ran a dating app, flikdate, by 2014. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Virtual-reality desktop and productivity software (Bellevue WA, its Form D address). 'Envelop VR has closed', announced 2017-01-11 (UploadVR). Its $4M round of October 2015 was led by Madrona (UploadVR; the Form D, amended February 2016, reports $5.55M sold with Madrona's Matt McIlwain as director); no source read names GV in a round, so the stage is undetermined.

Meeting-room and workplace software (Salt Lake City), renamed Teem: 'Teem started its operating life as Eventboard' (Sixteen:Nine, 2018-09-14). WeWork acquired Teem for $100M in September 2018 (TechCrunch, 2018-09-12). GV's round: EventBoard 'was previously backed by investors like Google Ventures and Marc Benioff' when Greycroft led its $6.5M round in November 2015 (TechCrunch); no source read names the round GV entered, so the stage is undetermined.

FaunaDB, a serverless operational database (San Francisco, its Form D address), founded by Twitter veterans. FaunaDB shut down in May 2025 (The Register, 2025-03-24). Country disputes the prefilled CZ claim, a one-word name match. Rounds: $3.1M sold in May 2016 and $21.75M of a $25M round in August 2017 (Form Ds; the 2017 one names Point72's Daniel Gwak as director), then $27M in July 2020, 'technically an extension of the company's 2017 Series A', led by Madrona with GV participating (TechCrunch, 2020-07-01). GV held the company by October 2017 (the firm's listing), and no source read says whether it entered at the 2016 round or the 2017 Series A, so the stage is undetermined.

Favor is The Pill Club (heyfavor.com; 'Favor, Formerly Known as The Pill Club', Femtech Insider, 2022-09-06), a birth-control and women's telehealth company in San Carlos CA (TechCrunch, 2019-01-22). GV came in as a new investor in the $51M Series B led by VMG Partners (TechCrunch, 2019-01-22) and was an existing investor in the $41.9M Series B extension of June 2021. The company filed for bankruptcy in April 2023 (Bloomberg) and Thirty Madison bought its assets in June 2023 (Fierce Healthcare); heyfavor.com now serves Nurx, 'a Thirty Madison company' (read 2026-09-28). Insolvency followed by an asset sale reads acquired. Status and country dispute the prefilled defunct and FR, a one-word name match on another Favor.

Florence (florenceos.com, which now redirects to fabrichealth.com), founded in 2021 to cut emergency-department operating costs, New York. It launched with a '$20M Seed Round Led by Thrive Capital, GV, and Salesforce Ventures' (PR Newswire, 2023-03-30), bought Zipnosis from Bright Health in May 2023 (Healthcare Dive), and renamed itself Fabric in 2024 (the company's own history page). Fabric's $60M Series A of 2024-02-27, led by General Catalyst with GV participating (the company's own post), graduates the seed. Operating as Fabric, a care-access platform. Country disputes the prefilled MA claim, a one-word name match. The sibling rows are filed under the new name (Thrive and General Catalyst, 'fabric': private, New York; aligned); the Redpoint and YC rows named Fabric are other companies. No priced mark near $1B is on record.

Flux Factory (flux.io), the first Google X spinout, collaborative building-design software, San Francisco (TechCrunch, 2015-12-21). Status and figure dispute the prefilled public row and its $55.8M float, a same-name registrant; country disputes the CZ claim. The 8VC, Bain Capital Ventures and Headline rows named Flux are other companies (flux.ai; a UK receipts fintech). GV's round: the $8M led by DFJ with Borealis, a16z, Google Ventures and Ev Williams (TechCrunch, 2014-05-06), the company's only round before the $29M 'Series B' of December 2015, so the record names it the Series A (model). Flux shut its tool suite on 2018-03-31 to pivot to a product for real estate professionals (The Architect's Newspaper, 2018-02-26); no source read gives the company's later fate and flux.io no longer answers, so status is unknown.

funding_rounds.round: unnamed ($8M, the Series A by the record)

note: Free (ffrree.com), an app to share real-time availability with friends, co-founded by Danny Trinh (ex-Path) and Kelvin Kakugawa; it 'raised $1.9 million from top seed funds like Social+Capital, Google Ventures, Lowercase, First Round, and SV Angel' (TechCrunch, 2015-06-11): its only round, seed-sized and described as a seed (model: Seed). Status and country dispute the prefilled acquired and FR: the Wikidata match is Free, the French telecom brand, another company. No source read gives this app's fate, so status is unknown; the First Round row (the same company, First Round is in the round) carries the same wrong acquired. City San Francisco as in the First Round row (model). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Glimpse (itsglimpse.com), a 2014 iOS app to meet people through Instagram, backed by 'First Round Capital, Google Ventures, Sherpa Ventures, Undercurrent Ventures, William Lauder and various angels' (The Next Web, 2014-08-01). Status and figure dispute the prefilled public row and its $41M float, which belong to The Glimpse Group (NASDAQ: VRAR). The First Round row is the same company (unknown there too); the 8VC row (a CPG company) and the Greylock row (a 2005 shopping site) are other companies. No source read names GV's round or gives the company's fate; the domain now hosts an unrelated dating site. No source places its office.

Greenwork (joingreenwork.com) connects young tradespeople with jobs and training for decarbonization work; its site is live (© 2026, read 2026-09-28). No source read names GV's round or places its office.

On-demand home cleaning (San Francisco, YC 2010); shut down on 2015-07-31 (Wikipedia). GV was not in the $1.7M seed of March 2013 (a16z, First Round and angels; TechCrunch). The $38M announced 2013-12-05 came in 'a Series A led by Google Ventures and a Series B led by Redpoint Ventures' (TechCrunch); Wikipedia's line that Google Ventures led the Series B contradicts that contemporary report, and the First Round row agrees with TechCrunch.

Humanoid, a 'human brainpower API' for crowdsourced tasks, came out of SpeakerText (a New York issuer on its 2010 Form D). After SpeakerText's $600K angel round (February 2011), 'Google Ventures is putting in a few hundred thousand dollars in another seed round' (TechCrunch, 2011-11-02). CloudFactory acquired SpeakerText and Humanoid in October 2012 (TechCrunch, 2013-03-03), which confirms the prefilled acquired. Country disputes the prefilled NL claim, a one-word name match; no source read places Humanoid's own office in 2011-12. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Jetpack.io (Devbox, Testpilot), founded by Daniel Loreto; 'Jetify Inc., formerly Jetpack Technologies Inc.' (jetpack.io, read 2026-09-28). Its '$10 million seed' was 'co-led by Coatue and GV' (TechCrunch, 2023-02-01); Jetify launched Testpilot in January 2025 (TechCrunch). GC AI, a legal-AI company, acquired Jetify in August 2026 (Law.com headline, 2026-08-10: https://www.law.com/legaltechnews/2026/08/10/gc-ai-acquires-backend-software-company-jetify-to-compete-with-big-tech-ai-platforms/), which aligns with the Coatue row ('Acq. by GC AI, 2026'). No later priced round was found. City San Francisco, as in the Coatue row (model). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Music-learning apps (Simply Piano), renamed Simply in July 2022 (Wikipedia). GV led a $50M round at a $1B valuation in June 2021 with Qualcomm Ventures and Hearst Ventures (Globes and Calcalist, 2021-06-21), its first investment: the company had raised '$43 million in three funding rounds' before it (Calcalist), a $5M Series A in 2014 among them (Wikipedia), so the round reads Growth. Mark: $1B exactly, at the band edge, and older than 24 months (stale); Wikipedia's $97M raised to date shows no later priced round. Israeli company, all 100 staff in Israel (Calcalist); the prefilled IL is confirmed from the company's own record.

Wi-Fi cold-press juicer (San Francisco); ceased operations in September 2017 (Wikipedia). Artis Ventures led the $70M Series B of March 2016, and 'Juicero's Series A and B investors included Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, GV (formerly Google Ventures), Thrive Capital' and others (TechCrunch, 2016-03-31), which does not say whether GV entered at the A or the B; its Form Ds ($4M from 2013-09-11, $15.9M from 2014-03-28, filed from New York) name no GV director, and no other source read separates the rounds, so the stage is undetermined.

Mobile messaging and social app by Keith Teare (Palo Alto, its Form D address). It 'raised $600,000 in seed funding' from Google Ventures, True Ventures, SV Angel, Betaworks and others (TechCrunch, 2011-07-29), then a $2.7M Series A led by Khosla Ventures (TechCrunch, 2011-12-29), which graduates the seed. Out of cash and owing Hercules $1.5M, it auctioned its assets in late 2013 and Teare's new entity, Just.me 2014 Inc., won them to keep the service running (TechCrunch, 2013-12-03): an asset sale out of insolvency reads acquired, with that successor.

Group sharing app turned web and mobile collaboration platform for small and medium businesses, founded 2011 by Matt Cutler and David Greenstein, on Business Insider's list of Boston startups (2013-04-02). It 'raised a $1 million round of seed funding from Google, CRV, General Catalyst' and others (TechCrunch, 2012-03-29; the headline calls it Google Ventures-backed). kibits.com no longer serves the product, and no source read gives the company's fate. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Rent-to-own homeownership (New York). GV led the $40M Series B, 'joined by Sequoia Capital' and others (TechCrunch, 2022-10-18), after the $165M equity and debt round of July 2021 backed by Sequoia, Jay-Z and Will Smith (TechCrunch headline, 2021-07-27); landis.com is live (© 2026 Landis Technologies Inc.). Momentum slice check 2026-09-28: no priced round at or near $1B on the record; the valuation was not disclosed. Aligned with the Sequoia row (private, below $1B, New York).

Last (last.co), a stealth mobile product 'that will make it more fun to go out and explore', on the firm's 2014-15 listings (partners Kevin Rose, then MG Siegler). Country disputes the prefilled NL claim, a one-word name match: nothing ties this company to the Netherlands, and the firm's deal partners were Bay Area consumer investors (model: US). A web search found no trace of the company, its round, its office or its fate.

Clothing-rental subscription (San Francisco, YC S13). Seed from Y Combinator, the YC-VC fund, 500 Startups, Andreessen Horowitz, Lerer Ventures and Google Ventures (TechCrunch, 2013-07-31); the $8.8M Series A led by Azure (TechCrunch, 2015-02-05) graduates it. Le Tote and Lord & Taylor filed for Chapter 11 on 2020-08-02 and the court approved the $12M sale of their intellectual property and e-commerce platforms to Saadia Group on 2020-10-20 (Wikipedia; Bloomberg Law); 'Saadia Group purchased Le Tote and Lord & Taylor' and ran the rental service until it went offline in spring 2024 (Yahoo Finance, 2024-04-18). Insolvency followed by an asset sale reads acquired, with that successor. The a16z, General Catalyst and YC rows read defunct without the sale; this row holds the cited sale. Sources: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/bankruptcy-law/lord-taylor-le-tote-12-million-asset-sale-to-saadia-approved ; https://finance.yahoo.com/news/effectively-defunct-le-tote-loses-143000078.html.

Light Labs (Palo Alto), multi-lens computational cameras (the L16), pivoted in 2020 to depth perception for vehicles. GV entered at the $30M Series C of July 2016, 'led by GV' (Wikipedia; TechCrunch, 2016-07-06), after a $9.7M Series A (2014) and a $25M round led by Formation 8 (2015); SoftBank's Vision Fund led the $121M Series D in July 2018 (TechCrunch). 'In May 2022, the tractor maker John Deere acquired parts of Light and hired some of the former staff' (Wikipedia): an asset sale of the business's technology, read as acquired. Country disputes the prefilled JP claim, a one-word name match; the Atomico, Balderton and Cherry rows named Light are a Copenhagen finance platform, another company.

RNA-targeting gene therapies, 'founded in 2016 and based in San Diego', later Locanabio. ARCH led the $55M Series A of 2019-05-22 with existing investors Temasek and Lightstone; 'New investors include UCB Ventures and GV' (the company's release). Locanabio said it would 'discontinue Locanabio's company operations by the end of 2023' while seeking homes for its programs (Fierce Biotech, 2023-11-02); no sale of the company followed on the record, so defunct. Source: https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/locanabio-looking-new-homes-genetic-medicines-operations-set-cease-end-year.

Marketing tools for local businesses (AngelPad-incubated; CEO Saumil Mehta, ex-Kosmix). It 'raised $5.1 million in Series A funding' led by InterWest Partners 'with participation from Google Ventures, Accel Partners, and 500 Startups' (TechCrunch, 2012-10-31); the firm has no post and no earlier round names GV. Its co-founder and CTO's bio reads 'LocBox (acquired by Square)' (Crunchbase News, 2024-03-13: https://news.crunchbase.com/startups/ai-solopreneur-staff-ramakrishnan-rocketship-vc/); the date and terms are not on the record. No source read places its office.

Lucidchart and Lucidpress, visual collaboration software, South Jordan UT (its 2020 Form D; Draper UT on the 2014 one). Status and figure dispute the prefilled public row and its $2.7B float, a same-name registrant joined on the name (cik_weak): Lucid is private. Mark aligned with the ICONIQ row (rule 10): in June 2021 Alkeon, Tiger Global and Steadfast bought more than $500M of stock at a $3B valuation (the company's release, 2021-06-24), the last priced event on record, though a secondary; the last primary, the $52M Series D led by ICONIQ in April 2020, valued it 'north of $1 billion' (Deseret News, 2020-04-16). Either way 1b_plus; the mark is older than 24 months (stale). Entry: the firm listed Lucid in 2014-16 (partner Dave Munichiello); the company's rounds are a $1M angel round in 2011, $4.36M sold from 2014-03-21 (Form D, Kickstart's Gavin Christensen a director), the $72M Series C of October 2018 and the Series D, and no source read names GV in any of them (the 2021 release lists Spectrum, ICONIQ, Meritech, Grayhawk and Kickstart as existing investors), so the stage is undetermined.

Mesh Wi-Fi routers (Atlanta). After a seed from Relay and Felicis and a $12.5M Series A co-led by Accel and Amazon in April 2016 without GV (TechCrunch), a16z and GV put in $7M in September 2016, which TechCrunch's correction calls 'a convertible note into the Series B' (TechCrunch, 2016-09-14): GV's entry is the Series B, Growth. First Alert (Newell Brands) acquired Luma in January 2018 (TechCrunch, 2018-01-12). Aligned with the a16z and Felicis rows (acquired); the Luma AI row in the a16z book is another company.

funding_rounds.round: convertible note into the Series B

note: In-game product placement. 'MediaSpike has raised a seed round of funding from Raptor Ventures, Venture51, Team Downey, Google Ventures, 500 Startups' and others (TechCrunch, 2012-08-03); CMEA led the $5.2M Series A with existing investors 500 Startups, Google Ventures and Raptor (TechCrunch, 2013-11-04; the Form D reports $5.09M sold from 2013-10-22), which graduates the seed. City: Mountain View, the address on its 2013-14 Form Ds (the a16z row says Palo Alto, uncited). No source read gives its fate; aligned with the a16z row (unknown).

Autonomous flight (Boston, offices in Los Angeles, Denver and New Zealand; TechCrunch, 2022-07-13). It raised '$3.5 million in seed funding and $21.5 million in Series A, led by First Round Capital and GV (formerly Google Ventures) respectively' (TechCrunch, 2021-05-26), and GV followed in the $105M Series B of July 2022. It listed through a merger with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. IV (prospectus 424B3 of 2026-02-12, principal offices 129 South Street, Boston; closing announced 2026-03-16, GlobeNewswire) and trades on Nasdaq as MRLN: market cap $176.87M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com). The First Round row's $257.75M is a 2025-06-30 float and the General Catalyst row reads unknown; this row holds the fresher cap.

funding_rounds.round: SPAC merger and PIPE (Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. IV)

note: Miso, the social TV check-in app by Bazaar Labs (San Francisco). 'The startup had previously raised seed funding last May from angel investors and from Google Ventures' (TechCrunch, 2011-01-04, on the $1.5M round Google Ventures led); Khosla then put in $4M with existing investors Google Ventures and Hearst (TechCrunch, 2011-12-01). Dijit bought Miso, 'the tie-up is complete' (TechCrunch, 2013-02-01), so acquired; the Khosla row reads defunct although its own note cites the Dijit deal. The YC rows named Miso (a Seoul home-services marketplace; Miso Labs) and Miso Robotics are other companies. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Music-learning apps (Miso Music, TechCrunch Disrupt 2010 People's Choice, Shark Tank 2012). It 'closed a $600K seed funding round led by Google Ventures' (TechCrunch, 2010-12-17), then $2.4M led by Mind Fund with Aria Ventures and Detroit Venture Partners, 'the company's second round of funding' (TechCrunch, 2011-09-14), which Market Realist names: 'raised $2.4 million in a Series A funding round that included Google' (2022-06-30). The named Series A graduates the seed (medium: a retrospective names it, the 2011 report does not). The company 'ran out of money, laid off most of its staff, and closed down in March 2013' (Market Realist; Inc. headline, 2014-02-28). No source read places its office.

Collaborative mobile video app from YouTube's co-founders; in 2014 AVOS turned into a single company working only on MixBit, with offices in New Zealand and San Mateo (TechCrunch, 2014-06-06). MixBit ceased operations on 2018-08-21 (Wikipedia). No source read names a round or GV's investment beyond the firm's listing, so the stage is undetermined.

One-touch conference dialing and calendar app (Boulder CO, its Form D address). 'As of 2021, MobileDay has shut down' (mobileday.com, read 2026-09-28). Form Ds: $1.03M sold from 2012-11-15 (Brad Feld a director), $1.5M from 2013-11-08 and $6.58M from 2014-07-11; the firm listed it from May 2013, and no source read ties GV to one of these rounds, so the stage is undetermined.

Family crafting and party-planning apps, co-founded by Soleil Moon Frye and Kara Nortman (Los Angeles, its Form D address). It announced '$2.5 million in funding led by GRP Partners with participation from Greycroft, Daher Capital, and Google Ventures' (TechCrunch, 2013-04-25; the Form D reports $2.72M sold from 2013-04-04): its first round, unnamed and just above the era's seed ceiling, so the stage is undetermined. No source read gives its fate.

Used-furniture consignment marketplace (San Francisco, YC W14). Its '$2.8 million seed round' was led by First Round and Index 'Other participants include Google Ventures' (TechCrunch, 2014-06-09). Metamorphic led a $9M round with Google Ventures in February 2015 (TechCrunch, 2015-02-12), unnamed but above twice the seed and $5M, so the seed graduated. It 'ceased operations' in June 2016, selling only its customer list to Handy (TechCrunch, 2016-06-29).

mytable (mytable.org), 'a marketplace and delivery service for locally cooked meals' on the firm's 2016 listing only. No source read names the company's round, office or fate; the domain serves no content.

Nearby (nearbyhq.com), 'the best independent shops in your town, all together', on the firm's 2021-22 listings. Status and city follow the Redpoint row (defunct, Oakland; its own card dates a 2021 Series A); no source read names GV's round, so the stage is undetermined.
